evidence.claims: Checked each Results bullet against results.txt and my recomputation: 'beats the untuned band and both fixed states on both held-out sets under both choice sets, by 0.01 to 0.06 C' (0.048/0.051 ours, 0.059/0.014 ref) pass; oracle gaps 0.009 worse / 0.010 better (ours), 0.024 better / equal (ref) pass; same band both sets, 4 and 2 of 54 within 0.02 C pass; tuned beats oracle on train 0.880 vs 0.920 pass; switch counts pass; 'at 20 C (ref) all gates and fixed closed score the same' pass (1.876/1.574 everywhere); 'a still narrower band might score slightly better' true (33.68-33.70 gives 0.871 vs 0.880, see domain). 'ref' = pythermalcomfort 4.6.1 confirmed. Limitations are frank (zero lag/cost, close-relative held-out rooms, proxy not comfort index, grid widened once). Not disclosed: whether the grid widening from 0.2 to 0.1 C was decided after seeing held-out numbers, and that the 33.7 C target is activity-independent.
evidence.fitness: Field: building physics / thermal comfort, specifically control of adaptive (IR-gating) textiles in a Gagge two-node model. Nearest prior work: on-off/hysteresis (deadband) control theory (Astrom & Murray, Feedback Systems, relay control; ASHRAE Handbook HVAC Applications ch. 48 on deadband), dynamic IR-gating textiles (Zhang et al. 2019 Science 363:619; Hsu et al. 2016 Science 353:1019 for static IR-transparent textiles), personal comfort systems and model-based control (Zhang, Arens et al. 2015 Build. Environ. 91:15; Kim et al. 2018 personal comfort models), and the Gagge two-node / pythermalcomfort implementation. Novelty is low: with zero lag, free switching and a score that is mean |tsk - set point| on the very variable the gate senses, the optimal on/off policy is bang-bang at the set point for any room, so a narrow band at 33.7 C 'carrying over' to held-out rooms is close to guaranteed by construction rather than evidence of generalisation. My scratch run confirms the optimum is a grid-boundary solution (bands 33.65-33.70 0.874, 33.68-33.70 0.871, 33.70-33.70 0.872 ours; 0.4568/0.4562 ref, all better than the reported 'tuned' 33.6-33.7). Effect sizes (0.01 to 0.06 C) are far below the two-node model's error against people (typically several tenths of a degree in mean skin temperature). Baselines are good (untuned, two fixed states, an oracle); confounds of actuation are disclosed, not handled. A useful robustness extension I ran: retuning at lag 5 and 10 min keeps the held-out advantage over the untuned band (ours 0.876 vs 0.922 and 0.918 vs 0.969 between; lag.out), which the README says was not run. A researcher can build on the code; the result itself is a small incremental step.
evidence.domain: The two-node model matches pythermalcomfort 4.6.1 to 1e-4 C (sound). The departure a comfort reviewer would flag: the score uses a fixed 33.7 C skin target in both phases, but ISO 7730 / Fanger (1970) give the comfortable mean skin temperature as 35.7 - 0.028 (M - W): 34.07 C at 1 met and 32.44 C at 2 met, so walking at 33.7 C is scored 'neutral' while it is about 1.3 C warm by the standard the repo's own base.pmv uses. Re-scoring with that activity-dependent target (fanger.py) leaves the ranking mostly intact under 'ours' (tuned 1.603/1.576/1.975 vs default 1.650/1.624/1.976) but under 'ref' retuning picks 33.8-33.9 and the untuned band beats it on the outside set (1.280 vs 1.282), and absolute errors roughly double, so the gate is far from the comfort target. No comfort index (PMV, SET, Zhang sensation) is used, and the README acknowledges that. A reviewer would not sign off on the method for a comfort claim; it is acceptable as a control-protocol exercise.

verdict: Computationally correct and honestly written: every number in the README reproduces byte-identically, an independent re-implementation of the gate, score, grid search and oracle and my own two-node model match to 3-4 dp, and the 'ref' model matches pythermalcomfort 4.6.1 to 1e-4 C. It does not meet the bar because verification is 2 (no test pins a headline number; 3 of 5 seeded mutants survive), and fitness and domain are 2: the 'tuned band carries over to held-out rooms' result is close to guaranteed by a zero-lag, zero-cost hysteresis gate scored on distance of its own sensed variable from the set point (the optimum sits at the grid boundary), and the fixed 33.7 C target departs from the ISO 7730 activity-dependent comfortable skin temperature. Finished (completeness 3). A lag-5/10 retune I ran shows the held-out advantage persists, which would strengthen the next step.
